newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Arabian shares down 1.8 percent in week.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabian shares down 1.8 percent in week.

text.p: Saudi Arabian stocks ended 1.8 percent weaker in thinner trade last week, figures from the Riyadh-based Bakheet Financial Advisors (BFA) showed on Sunday.
The index closed at 151.07 points on Thursday from 153.85 the previous week. Of the 59 companies traded, 11 rose, 34 fell and 14 were unchanged.

Banks accounted for 29 percent of trading volume, which BFA said edged down to 3.24 million shares worth 666 million riyals ($177 million) from nearly 3.79 million shares worth almost 910 million riyals.
For the third week running, Riyad Bank was the most active share. It accounted for some 20 percent of value traded and closed two percent weaker at 238 riyals, BFA figures show.
Another active stock was Saudi Basic Industries Corp, which closed two percent down at 398 riyals.
In a correction after the previous week's 15 percent jump to 82 riyals, SCECO-Southern was the biggest loser in the week, sliding 8.5 percent to 75 riyals.
Banking heavyweight Saudi American Bank lost 5.5 percent to 567 riyals and Beshah Agricultural Development Co was two riyals weaker at 36.
Among the week's gainers were Saudi Advanced Industries Co, which was four riyals firmer at 57 and Tabuk Agriculture Development Co, which was five riyals better at 90. ($1=3.75 riyals)
